complexity.notes: Correctness is fragile: the constraints allow any of 256 ASCII characters, so an input string could literally contain the delimiter and corrupt the decode; a length-prefix scheme (e.g. 'len#string') is the robust standard approach. Works only because real inputs are unlikely to contain the magic string. Also, decode relies on the trailing delimiter to make pop(-1) valid, which is a bit subtle.
complexity.summary: Encodes by joining all strings with a long fixed literal delimiter (plus a trailing delimiter) and decodes by splitting on that delimiter and dropping the final empty piece. Both join and split are linear in the total character volume, which scales linearly with n.
